title: How to explain gaps in your CV (with examples)
desc: How to explain gaps in your CV: one honest line, what you did with the time, and a short answer ready for interview. UK examples for every common reason.
blocks: p

If you are wondering how to explain gaps in your CV, the short answer is this: name the gap in one honest line, add anything useful you did during that time, and have a 20 second answer ready for interview. Employers see gaps every week. What worries them is a gap that looks hidden.
p

The National Careers Service says much the same: a gap is not a problem in itself, but you might be asked about it. Below you will find wording for the most common reasons, the mistakes that cause real damage, and what the law says about health.
h2
Do UK employers really care about gaps in a CV?
p

Less than you fear. A few months between jobs barely registers with most recruiters, because job hunting takes time. A gap of a year or more will usually prompt a question, either on a screening call or at interview.
p

The real risk is not the gap. It is dates that do not add up. If your CV says one thing, your application form another and your reference a third, the recruiter starts wondering what else is unclear. So my firm advice: never stretch the dates of the job before or after to cover a gap. A neutral fact becomes a trust problem the moment a reference check disagrees with you.
h2
Should you put the reason for a gap on your CV?
p

For a gap longer than about six months, yes, in one line. Save the detail for your cover letter or the interview. Shorter gaps rarely need a label at all, especially if you show years only (2022 to 2024) rather than months. That is common on UK CVs, as long as you do it for every job.
p
Here is how the most frequent reasons look in practice. The wording is only an example: adapt it to your situation.

h2
How do I explain a gap after redundancy or being dismissed?
p

Redundancy is the easy one, even if it does not feel that way. Your role ended for business reasons, so say so plainly: "My role was made redundant when the company closed its regional office." No apology, no bitterness. Recruiters know that redundancies happen to good people.
p

Dismissal is harder, and the National Careers Service suggests it is better discussed at interview than written on your CV. Keep the explanation brief, say what you learned and what you do differently now. Do not criticise your former employer, even if you feel badly treated: the interviewer only hears someone who might one day talk about them that way.
h2
Do I have to tell an employer about health reasons for a gap?
p

No. You decide how much to share. Under section 60 of the Equality Act 2010, which applies in England, Scotland and Wales, an employer must not ask about your health before offering you work, apart from limited exceptions (for example, to check whether you need adjustments for an assessment, or whether you can carry out a function that is intrinsic to the job).
p

In practice, "Career break for personal reasons" is a perfectly acceptable line. If you want to say more, keep it short and forward-looking: "I took time out for health reasons and I am now fully able to work."
h2
What can I add to a gap to make my CV look stronger?
p
A gap with something in it reads very differently from an empty one. You do not need anything impressive, only something true:
ul
Volunteering: a charity shop shift, a food bank, a school or sports club committee.
Courses: a short or online course, with its name and the year. It shows you are willing to learn.
Caring skills: managing appointments, budgets or paperwork for someone else is real organisation.
Odd jobs and freelance work: a few weeks of temping, tutoring or bar work counts.
Personal projects: a website, a small online shop, a renovation you planned and costed.
ex
2023 to 2024: Unemployed
2023 to 2024: Career break, caring for a parent. Completed a food hygiene certificate and volunteered weekly at a local food bank, managing stock and the volunteer rota.
p
If you are coming back after a long break with little paid work behind you, our guide on how to write a CV with no work experience shows how to lead with skills, education and volunteering instead.
h2
What mistakes make a CV gap look worse?
ul
Changing dates. The single most damaging mistake, because it is easy to check.
Over-explaining. A paragraph about a difficult year draws more attention than one calm line.
Apologising. "Unfortunately I was out of work" sounds defensive. State the fact.
Hiding dates altogether. A CV with no dates at all makes recruiters assume the worst.
Forgetting the application form. Many forms ask for a full employment history with every gap explained. Keep your answers consistent with your CV.
h2
What should I say about a gap in a job interview?
p
Use three short parts: what happened, what you did, and why you are ready now. Then stop talking. The longer you go on, the more it sounds like a problem.
ex
"Well, it was a difficult time, there were a lot of things going on at home and it took longer than I expected to sort everything out..."
"I took 18 months out to care for my mother. During that time I kept my bookkeeping skills up to date with an online course. Her care is now arranged, and I am looking for a full-time role."
p
One sentence in your cover letter can also do the work before the interview even starts. Our guide on how to write a cover letter shows where it fits.

faq
Quick answers about CV gaps
Is a six month gap on a CV a problem?
Rarely. Many recruiters will not even ask. If they do, a one-sentence answer about job hunting, a course or a personal reason is enough.
Can I just leave a gap off my CV?
You can show years instead of months, which hides short gaps naturally. Do not change dates or remove a job to close a gap, and remember that application forms often ask for your full history.
Should I mention a gap in my cover letter?
Only if it is long or recent, and in one sentence. Explain the reason briefly and move on to why you fit the job.
